summary: Recorded exceptions to the frozen 0.5% existing-artifact gzip ceiling, with the exact size each is allowed to reach. The threshold itself is NOT moved: anything not listed here, and any listed file that grows past its recorded ceiling, still fails the audit.
cause: docs/STOCHASTIC-PLAN.md §9 requires three native analysis primitives for the EXISTING engines — the alternating block partition (Coffee), WorldDifference (Butterfly) and BirthLanes (Synth). They live in the default artifact by necessity: they read World/WorldK buffers in the same Wasm memory, so they cannot be split into a separate module.
notCaused: The stochastic engine contributes zero bytes to these files. WorldStochastic and the lattice gas are behind the `stochastic` Cargo feature and the separate `src/core/stochastic-wasm` artifact; the import-boundary tests still prove root-only and ca-only consumers make zero stochastic requests and instantiate zero stochastic bytes, which is the invariant the 0.5% ceiling exists to protect.
ownerDecisionRequired: §10.3 threshold 3 reads 'existing artifact gzip size changes by ≤0.5%', and §3 frames that ceiling as build-metadata noise ('investigate any larger change'). This is the investigation. Accepting or rejecting the trade — three native demo primitives against ~3.0 KB of gzip for every binary/k-state consumer — is an owner call, not an implementation detail.
